text:
arya: odd bug — interactive `redwoodctl login` works but our CI picks up a different profile and fails. digging I found a file /tmp/redwood-completion-config.json and CI was reading that. didn't create it myself. anyone seen completion scripts leaking envs?

mike: can you show `env | grep REDWOOD` and the completion you source? maybe a completion helper created a temp file.

arya: output:
```
$ env | grep REDWOOD
REDWOOD_CONFIG=/tmp/redwood-completion-config.json
```
I only source fish completion from the package: `fish_add_path (redwoodctl --completion=fish)` in my config.

trina: oof. older fish completions sometimes wrote temp files and exported vars for helpers. if that temp file is exported it will persist for the session and any child process (including CI runners that inherit the env). not great.

mike: can you cat the completion file? `redwoodctl --completion=fish` should print a function, not export REDWOOD_CONFIG.

arya:
```
# output of redwoodctl --completion=fish
function __redwood_config
  set -l cfg (mktemp -t redwood-completion-config.json)
  echo '{"profiles":{}}' > $cfg
  set -x REDWOOD_CONFIG $cfg
end
complete -c redwoodctl -f -a '(__redwood_config ; redwoodctl _complete_cmds)'
```
there's the bug: `set -x` exports the var globally for the fish session.

devex-bot: Known issue: older completion generator emitted `set -x` for fish which exports envvars. See issue #400 in our completions repo.

mike: yep that's the leak. Fixes: 1) completion should use `set -l` (local) and not `set -x`, or write a helper that runs in a subshell so env doesn't leak. 2) CLI should avoid treating REDWOOD_CONFIG pointing to /tmp as authoritative — treat it as suspect and prefer $XDG_CONFIG_HOME unless `REDWOOD_CONFIG` explicitly set by user (and not in /tmp). 3) Add a `redwoodctl doctor` check that warns if REDWOOD_CONFIG is under /tmp.

arya: quick repro for CI: we run `fish -c 'source ~/.config/fish/completions/redwoodctl.fish; redwoodctl auth status'` in a container and it inherits the exported REDWOOD_CONFIG. workaround for now: `env -u REDWOOD_CONFIG redwoodctl auth status` or `unset -n REDWOOD_CONFIG` before running.

trina: I'll open PR to change completion generator: replace `set -x` with `set -l tmp_cfg` and then call helper with `env REDWOOD_CONFIG=$tmp_cfg redwoodctl _complete_cmds` so the CLI sees it only for completion. Also adding a test that generated completion doesn't export envs in an interactive session.

mike: I'll also add a defensive check: if REDWOOD_CONFIG starts with /tmp or /var/folders on macOS, CLI prints a one-line warning: "REDWOOD_CONFIG appears to point to a transient file; ignoring for non-interactive shells. Use --config to explicitly set." and fallback to XDG path when running non-interactively. We'll need to be careful about breaking scripts that intentionally set REDWOOD_CONFIG — opt-out with REDWOOD_CONFIG_FORCE=1.

arya: filed ISSUE: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/812 — title: "fish completion exports REDWOOD_CONFIG via set -x; causes temp config leak to CI". attached snippet and suggested fix. PR incoming from trina. thanks folks, that explains the flaky CI runs we've had for two weeks.

devex-bot: CI note: added temporary CI script to unset REDWOOD_CONFIG before running redwoodctl tests to avoid flakes.

mike: good catch. I'll add a changelog entry and a little note in the completion docs about not exporting envvars.

arya: confirmed: `env -u REDWOOD_CONFIG` fixes CI. will wait for the PR. :thumbsup:
